mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X gives N potatoes to Y", immediately subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's current count, respecting the order of statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement appears in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Updating the giver's count after a later transfer instead of at the point of the statement, leading to incorrect totals.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "has K more than"
mathgap.principle: Interpret "A has K more than B" as the signed equation A − B = K (or A = B + K), preserving the order and allowing K to be negative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a comparative statement uses the phrase "has K more than".
mathgap.example: Swapping A and B and writing B − A = K, which yields the opposite relationship.

mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form "The number of potatoes that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of potatoes that C and D have", translate to (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order on both sides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement equates two differences.
mathgap.example: Treating the right‑hand side as |C − D| or swapping C and D, thereby losing the sign information.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "difference between X and Y"
mathgap.principle: Read "difference between the number of X and Y" as the signed expression X − Y, keeping the order as stated.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a phrase "difference between X and Y" appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting it as the absolute difference |X − Y|, which discards sign information.

mathgap.title: Current‑Count Constraint for "has N"
mathgap.principle: A statement "A has N potatoes" fixes A's count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers or constraints have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a direct count statement appears.
mathgap.example: Treating "A has N" as the initial count regardless of earlier transfers, causing inconsistency with later constraints.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations, simplifying them and solving for any other variables that can now be determined.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After any equation yields a concrete value for a variable.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known value unused in later equations, missing the chance to resolve additional variables.

mathgap.title: Allow Negative Differences in Contradictory "more than" Phrases
mathgap.principle: If a "more than" phrase appears in a context that contradicts a previous comparison, allow the difference to be negative rather than assuming an error.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a "has K more than" statement conflicts with another relationship involving the same persons.
mathgap.example: Forcing K to be positive and rejecting a solution where the signed difference is negative.

mathgap.title: Consistency Check After Solving
mathgap.principle: After assigning values to all variables, verify each original statement—including transfers, direct counts, and comparative equations—to ensure they are all satisfied.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution without rechecking that a transfer statement balances both parties' counts.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after any earlier statements (including transfers and direct counts) have been applied.
mathgap.example: Using initial counts for a comparison that appears after a transfer, ignoring the effect of the transfer.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations that involve the queried person directly or through a chain of dependencies, and solve only that subsystem, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem includes many statements, before solving.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system including irrelevant variables, leading to unnecessary complexity and possible errors.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often treats the phrase as "B has K more than A" or writes the equation B − A = K, reversing the intended relationship.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map "A has K more than B" to A − B = K (or A = B + K) and keep the order of A and B as given.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The wording "difference between X and Y" is mistakenly read as |X − Y|, discarding sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "difference between X and Y" as the signed expression X − Y, preserving the order in the statement.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers out of sequence or assumes all transfers happen after all counts are set, breaking the temporal dependencies.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each "gives" statement in the order it appears, updating counts immediately before handling later statements.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes "A has N" always defines the starting amount, even when the statement occurs after transfers that should have already altered A's count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Use "A has N" to constrain A's current count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers or constraints.

mathgap.description: Assuming all "more than" differences must be positive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model enforces K > 0 for "has K more than" even when the logical relationship yields a negative signed difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow K to be negative when the surrounding equations dictate a negative signed difference; do not impose a positivity constraint.
